title: Crows can evaluate visual info twice as fast as mammals
summary: Birds' compact nervous system seems to help them handle tasks very quickly.
llm_summary: Crows process visual information up to twice as fast as mammals, thanks to their compact, highly efficient brains. This rapid visual‑processing ability lets them solve complex tasks—like recognizing objects or tracking moving prey—in a fraction of the time it takes a typical mammal. The findings highlight how avian neural architecture can outperform larger, more “traditional” nervous systems in speed‑critical computing.
